verses.text: Moreover Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah the second time, while he was yet shut up in the court of the guard, saying,
“Yahweh who does it, Yahweh who forms it to establish it; Yahweh is his name, says:
‘Call to me, and I will answer you, and will show you great things, and difficult, which you don’t know.’

For Yahweh, the God of Israel, says concerning the houses of this city, and concerning the houses of the kings of Judah, which are broken down to make a defense against the mounds and against the sword;

while men come to fight with the Chaldeans, and to fill them with the dead bodies of men, whom I have killed in my anger and in my wrath, and for all whose wickedness I have hidden my face from this city:
‘Behold, I will bring it health and cure, and I will cure them; and I will reveal to them abundance of peace and truth.
I will cause the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel to return, and will build them, as at the first.

I will cleanse them from all their iniquity, by which they have sinned against me; and I will pardon all their iniquities, by which they have sinned against me, and by which they have transgressed against me.

This city shall be to me for a name of joy, for a praise and for a glory, before all the nations of the earth, which shall hear all the good that I do to them, and shall fear and tremble for all the good and for all the peace that I procure to it.’”

Yahweh says: “Yet again there shall be heard in this place, about which you say, ‘It is waste, without man and without animal, even in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, that are desolate, without man and without inhabitant and without animal,’

the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who say, ‘Give thanks to Yahweh of Armies, for Yahweh is good, for his loving kindness endures forever;’ who bring thanksgiving into Yahweh’s house. For I will cause the captivity of the land to return as at the first,” says Yahweh.
Yahweh of Armies says: “Yet again shall there be in this place, which is waste, without man and without animal, and in all its cities, a habitation of shepherds causing their flocks to lie down.

In the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the lowland, and in the cities of the South, and in the land of Benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, shall the flocks again pass under the hands of him who counts them,” says Yahweh.
“Behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that I will perform that good word which I have spoken concerning the house of Israel and concerning the house of Judah.
“In those days, and at that time, I will cause a Branch of righteousness to grow up to David; and he will execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will dwell safely; and this is the name by which she shall be called: Yahweh our righteousness.”
For Yahweh says: “David shall never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel;
neither shall the priests the Levites want a man before me to offer burnt offerings, and to burn meal offerings, and to do sacrifice continually.”
Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah, saying,
“Yahweh says: ‘If you can break my covenant of the day, and my covenant of the night, so that there shall not be day and night in their season;
then may also my covenant be broken with David my servant, that he shall not have a son to reign on his throne; and with the Levites the priests, my ministers.
As the army of the sky can’t be counted, neither the sand of the sea measured; so I will multiply the offspring  of David my servant, and the Levites who minister to me.’”
Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah, saying,
“Don’t consider what this people has spoken, saying, ‘The two families which Yahweh chose, he has cast them off?’ Thus they despise my people, that they should be no more a nation before them.”
Yahweh says: “If my covenant of day and night fails, if I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth;

then I will also cast away the offspring  of Jacob, and of David my servant, so that I will not take of his offspring  to be rulers over the offspring  of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: for I will cause their captivity to return, and will have mercy on them.”

footnotes.content: Even locked away, Jeremiah hears the Lord again. Notice how many times God speaks to him in prison—it's as if the more the world closes doors, the more heaven opens them. That's a comfort I've learned to lean on.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Yahweh who does it"—the Lord names Himself as the One who *acts*, not merely speaks. He forms, establishes, is present. When my world felt like rubble, I found that name meant everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Call to me, and I will answer. Not someday—now. And He promises to show us not what we already know, but great and difficult things, hidden from us until we ask. That's the posture He's always wanted: our honest asking.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerusalem's houses torn down, its stones turned to ramparts—all the work of human hands defending against the Chaldeans. The Lord is about to speak into this wreckage and name what He will do instead.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The dead lie in the streets because of Judah's sin and God's just judgment. It's hard to read, but merciful too—He names the sickness plainly. Only then can healing come. He doesn't look away from what we've done.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Health, cure, peace, truth—not said once but twice, as if God Himself is amazed at what He means to do. After judgment, *abundance*. I've seen that rhythm in my own life: the hardest winters do end, and what grows back is often richer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Both Judah and Israel—the captive kingdoms, estranged. God speaks of their return as *one act*, as if the fracture itself will be healed. When you've been scattered, that promise of wholeness is the deepest mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cleansed from iniquity, pardoned—notice how it's repeated, *all* their iniquities. There's something tender in that repetition, as if God is determined we know He leaves nothing behind. The past will not haunt His restored people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This city—once defiled, now a name of joy. And the nations will see it and tremble, not in fear but in reverent wonder at what the Lord has done. That's how the world learns God is good: by watching Him restore those He loves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerusalem emptied, waste, silent—no one, no animal. That's what the people say. But the Lord is about to contradict that testimony with a different sound: not the silence of death, but the sounds of life and joy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The voices of bridegroom and bride—weddings, new life, new families beginning. And in their midst, the song: "His loving kindness endures forever." What a way to restore: not with silence, but with music and thanksgiving and the oldest human joy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shepherds again—the quiet, humble work of tending flocks. After siege and sword, the Lord brings back the pastoral peace. Sometimes restoration looks less like triumph and more like a man at rest with his sheep.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From hill country to lowland to South to Benjamin to Jerusalem—the *whole land*, named region by region, will know the shepherd's hand counting their flocks. That specificity matters: God restores not in theory but place by place, person by person.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Behold, the days come. A word Jeremiah has spoken many times in judgment; now he speaks it in hope. The good word—what Israel has longed for, what seems impossible in the wreckage. The Lord is keeping His promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A Branch of righteousness for David—and He will execute justice and righteousness. Readers today hear an echo in that Branch: the One whose kingdom rests on justice and peace without end. It is the hope that sustained even the remnant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Judah will be saved; Jerusalem will dwell safely. And her name: Yahweh our righteousness. Not her own, but His—that's the secret of true peace. When you know your security rests in Him, not in walls or weapons, you can finally breathe.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David shall never lack a man to sit on his throne. This isn't just about dynasty; it's about a line that will not be cut off. For Israel, that promise meant everything—their king, their inheritance, their future was bound up in it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priests, the Levites—they will not want for a man. Their service, their sacrifices will continue. The worship of God will not cease. In a restoration, it's vital: the people need not just to live, but to remember Whom they live for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Another word comes to Jeremiah—the Lord is not finished. He moves from the promise of restoration to the ground of it: the unchanging covenants He has made. Notice how deliberately He speaks in layers, each word confirming the last.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Break the covenant of day and night? It's absurd—the Sun rises and sets as it always has, the night falls as it always will. That's the Lord's point: some laws cannot be broken; they are written into creation itself. My covenant with David is like that.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If you break one covenant, then My covenant with David could be broken too. But the premise is impossible—you cannot unmake the sun and moon. So David's throne, David's son, will stand as surely as the heavens stand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As uncountable as the stars, as the sand of the sea—the offspring of David will multiply. It's a beautiful promise after exile and barrenness. And the Levites, God's ministers, will serve without end. Abundance replaces every loss.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Another word, another question to address: the people are speaking despair. They say God has cast off the two families—Israel and Judah. But despair is a liar. The Lord is about to contradict it entirely.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Don't listen to their spite—they're saying God has rejected both His chosen families, that they're no nation at all. It's not a small thing, to keep faith when the whole world, including your neighbors, declares you forsaken. But God declares otherwise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The covenant of day and night again—the ordinances of heaven and earth. The Lord appeals to the visible creation as His guarantee. As long as seasons turn and the heavens move, His covenant stands. It's the most steadfast oath I know.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will not cast away the seed of Jacob, of David. I will cause their captivity to return and have mercy. After all the trial, that's what matters: the Lord's mercy endures, and His people will come home. Not because they deserve it, but because He has bound Himself to them forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
